newsitem.title: UK: UK scraps Siemens-Plessey defence deal.
newsitem.headline: UK scraps Siemens-Plessey defence deal.

text.p: Britain's Ministry of Defence has decided to terminate its contract with Siemens Plessey Systems for an automated electronic warfare system, defence producement minister James Arbuthnot said on Monday.
He said tests carried out in 1995 and last year had shown that the company's Vixen system had "operational shortcomings".

Arbuthnot said the ministry was now considering its legal position and would, if appropriate, pursue a claim for compensation. He said the cost so far of the Vixen project had been around 50 million pounds ($80 million).
"The decision to cancel Vixen was taken only after careful consideration of the operational, contractual, financial and industrial implications," he said.

Arbuthnot said in a written parliamentary answer that various technical problems had delayed the Vixen project by several years. There was little prospect of these being overcome without further significant delay and expense.
The Vixen system was designed to collect and disseminate accurate signals intelligence from a high density, dynamic electronic environment.
A Ministry spokesman said he was unable to give a figure for the potential value of the contract to Siemens Plessey had it gone through to completion.
A spokesman for Siemens declined to comment. ($1=.6237 Pound)
